7-scenario isolated-fixture harness proving acquire creates and check/heartbeat/release never create

completion_data.completion_summary: Added an opt-in create-if-missing mode to resolve_task_dir, passed only by cmd_acquire and reachable only from a state.json-derived path attempted after the existing glob fallback, so acquire against a not_started task with no directory yet succeeds and creates reports/plans/summaries while check/heartbeat/release remain provably side-effect-free. Updated the canonical contract doc, deployed the source store, and proved the behavior with a 7-scenario isolated-fixture test plus a live probe against a real task.

memory_candidates.content: Some source-store scripts (this codebase's agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/*.sh) refuse direct execution outside a deployed .claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/ tree via a structural deploy-root-guard.sh check on the script's own directory path. To test such a script's behavior in an isolated fixture without touching the real deploy tree or real state, build a mktemp -d root containing a .claude/scripts/ subdirectory (copy of the deployed script plus its guard), and a synthetic specs/state.json -- the guard only checks the parent directory NAME pattern (*/.claude or */.opencode), so a throwaway temp root satisfies it without any real deploy. This is the sanctioned pattern for testing deploy-guarded scripts in this codebase.

When adding create-if-missing behavior to a resolver function with multiple resolution strategies (authoritative source lookup, then a fallback scan), attempt creation only AFTER every read-only fallback has been tried and failed, never inside an early branch that would short-circuit later fallbacks. Placing creation inside an early branch risks creating a second, divergent artifact when the authoritative source has drifted from what the fallback would have found (e.g. a renamed/relocated on-disk directory), silently splitting state across two locations instead of resolving the existing one.
